title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page finishes the theorem begun on p.138 and draws three corollaries.

**The theorem (p.138).** Take the half-plane D with the analytic family E_z = C/(Z·1 + Z·(−z̄)). This family is a universal cover of the analytic stack M_{1,1}^{an}. It classifies elliptic curves with a 'Torelli rigidification', meaning an oriented isomorphism u: Z^2 → π_E = H_1(E,Z). The group of M_{1,1}-automorphisms of D acts on the right and is identified with SL(2,Z), acting by Möbius transformations.

**Matching actions.** The first lines of this page state that this action matches the natural left action of SL(2,Z) on Torelli structures, g·u = u∘g^{-1}.

**Corollary 1.** There is a canonical isomorphism (26) T_{1,1} := π_1(M_{1,1}) ≅ SL(2,Z), with π_1 computed relative to the chosen universal cover D. Equivalently there is a canonical isomorphism of stacks (27) M_{1,1} ≅ [D / SL(2,Z)]. Note that SL rather than PSL is correct: −1 is the generic automorphism of every elliptic curve.

**Corollary 2.** Grothendieck then invokes 'les grands théorèmes ...'. The word is illegible, but these are presumably the Teichmüller-theoretic results identifying π_1(M_{g,ν}) with the Teichmüller (mapping class) group. From them he deduces the statement for a compact connected oriented pointed surface (E,a) of genus 1. Let T be the group of isotopy classes of (orientation-preserving) automorphisms of (E,a). Then the natural map T → Aut^+_Z(H), with H = π_1(E,a) ≅ Z^2, is an isomorphism. This is the classical MCG(T^2, pt) ≅ SL(2,Z).

**Corollary 3 (purely group-theoretic form).** Let π be a 'groupe à lacets' of type (1,1): the discrete fundamental group of a once-punctured torus, i.e. F_2 with its distinguished loop class around the puncture and its orientation. Let H = π^{ab} ≅ Z^2 and T = Autext^+_{lac}(π), the outer automorphisms preserving the loop class and the orientation. Then the map (28) T → Aut^+_Z(H) = SL(2,Z) is an isomorphism. This is essentially Nielsen's theorem Out(F_2) ≅ GL(2,Z), restricted to the orientation-preserving part.

**Margin note.** It is a to-do: one should make the action of Aut^+_Z(H) on π explicit, i.e. lift SL(2,Z) to explicit automorphisms of F_2 or of the pointed surface.

**Next page.** It goes on to describe the tangent bundle along the fibres and the universal cover of the associated principal C*-type bundle via exp(2iπz). This is the start of the passage to the Teichmüller-type universal cover of the punctured universal curve.

**Purpose.** This is part of Grothendieck's 'Teichmüller tower' programme for (g,ν) = (1,1). He describes π_1(M_{1,1}), the topological mapping class group, and the abstract 'lacet-group' outer automorphism group as one and the same object, with careful attention to left/right conventions and orientation.
errors: Corollary 3 says H = π^{ab} is 'libre de rang 1' (per the transcription). For a type (1,1) group (F_2) the abelianization is free of rank 2. This is either a slip or a misreading.
The equation number (27) is used twice: once for M_{11} ≅ (D, SL(2,Z)) and once for the map in Corollary 2.
Corollary 2 does not say explicitly that the automorphisms are orientation-preserving; this is needed to land in Aut^+. The marginal insertion 'orientée' and the superscript + handle it implicitly.

Deriving Corollary 2 from Corollary 1 relies on an unstated identification of π_1(M_{1,1}) with the mapping class group (Teichmüller theory). That identification is essentially equivalent to the conclusion, so as a 'deduction' it is circular unless the Teichmüller results are taken as given.

ideas.what: π_1 of the moduli stack M_{1,1} is canonically SL(2,Z), and M_{1,1} is the quotient stack [D/SL(2,Z)], with left/right action conventions via Torelli rigidifications
ideas.modern_name: orbifold/stack fundamental group of M_{1,1}; analytic uniformization of M_{1,1}
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Klein, Fricke); stack form folklore since Deligne–Mumford / Deligne–Rapoport era
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche discuss π_1(M_{g,ν}) = Teichmüller groups in general terms

ideas.what: Mapping class group of a pointed torus is SL(2,Z) via action on π_1
For the 'groupe à lacets' of type (1,1), the orientation- and loop-preserving outer automorphism group maps isomorphically to SL(2,Z)
ideas.modern_name: Nielsen's theorem Out(F_2) ≅ GL(2,Z), restricted to Out^+(F_2)
ideas.where_published: Autext_lac and groups of type (g,ν) appear in La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981) and Esquisse d'un programme (1984), in general form

deep.surprise_reason: Classical results (π_1(M_{1,1}) = SL(2,Z), MCG of the torus, Nielsen's Out(F_2)), written in Grothendieck's lacet-group language with careful conventions. Nothing new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: 'libre de rang 1' should mathematically read rang 2 (H = Z^2); check the manuscript, which may itself contain the slip.
'multiaux-points' is a dubious reading. Context suggests a reference to the big theorems of Teichmüller theory (or comparison theorems); the word is illegible and should be marked [?].
In the Corollary 3 heading, the marginal word reads 'orientation' and the inserted words 'lacet de type', i.e. 'groupe à lacets orienté de type (1,1)'.
The left marginal note reads roughly 'Il faudrait expliciter l'action de Aut^+_Z(H) sur π resp. ... Aut^+_Z(H) ...', a to-do about making the lifts of SL(2,Z) explicit.
